offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

proposed.why: Every metric sample and the money check contradict the alert. The ledger group's lag never went above 1, and the books reconcile, so the alert looks false.

diagnosis.hypothesis: The alert's symptom is not real. The alert says the ledger consumer group is 250 messages behind on provider-events, but the lag never got near that. For the last 30 minutes, the ledger group's lag was 0 at every minute, with a single 1-message peak at about 01:14. That includes the firing time, 01:16:31. The money check settled in 0.22s. All 1093 provider events were posted exactly once, the ledger is balanced, and payments and refunds all match the provider. So the ledger consumer is keeping up and nothing is stuck. The alert most likely fired on bad input: a stale or wrong lag value, a bad alert expression (for example a summing error, or the wrong label or group), or a test alert. It was not an actual backlog. What is still unknown is what the alerting system evaluated. I could not see the alert rule's expression or the history of its value, and I did not check deploys.

evidence.shows: Lag per consumer: ledger and payment-confirmer are both at 0 for every sample from 01:11 to 01:16, the firing time included.
The per-minute max of lag peaks at 1 for ledger (about 01:14:47), far below the threshold of 50 and the claimed 250. A spike between samples is ruled out.
Total lag across all groups and partitions is 0 or 1 throughout.

The money check passed and settled in 0.22s. All 1093 events were posted exactly once, the ledger is balanced at $58,648.04 each side, the ledger matches the provider, and all 1000 payments and 93 refunds match. The ledger is not behind.
The lag metric is labeled by consumer and partition, not group. An alert rule that filters or groups on a 'group' label, or on a different consumer name, would not be measuring this metric.

proposed_fix.summary: The system needs no change. Review the ConsumerLagHigh rule: check its expression, label selectors and data source against klaxon_kafka_consumer_lag{consumer="ledger"}. Also check whether the alert was a test or a manual fire. Correct the rule if it is wrong, and silence or resolve this alert.

diagnosis.blast_radius: None from the system side, because no service changes. Editing the alert rule could hide real lag if done wrong.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the alert rule is edited, restore its previous definition from version control.
